description: Fictional examples for evaluating candidate detection. These are not claims about real publications.

cases.text: The reckless and disastrous plan will leave families paying the price.
The council published its transport plan on Tuesday. The document contains 18 proposals and will be debated next month.
cases.notes: Neutral factual reporting; avoid forcing a technique label.

cases.text: We can either accept this proposal exactly as written or watch the entire service collapse.
cases.notes: Two options are presented as exhaustive and one is linked to a threatening outcome.

cases.text: If the bridge inspection finds structural damage, the council may close the crossing to protect the public.
cases.notes: A conditional safety warning is not automatically an appeal to fear.

cases.text: The report called the service 'unacceptable', but the next sentence said the issue had been resolved the previous day.
cases.notes: The quotation is contextualised; do not flag quote mining.
